title: Time & Days
description: Today and tomorrow, the parts of the day, and hours, days, weeks and years. Indonesian verbs don't change for time, so these words do that work instead.

items.registerNotes: It comes before a day's name: hari Senin (Monday). Tiga hari is three days.

items.pitfallNote: With a capital M, Minggu is also Sunday, so minggu depan is next week but hari Minggu depan is next Sunday.

items.registerNotes: Bulan ini is this month and bulan depan next month. The months' names are close to English: Januari, Maret, Agustus, Desember.
Tahun depan is next year and tahun lalu last year. For age: Umur saya tiga puluh tahun (I'm thirty).
Literally 'this day'. In the same way, minggu ini is this week and tahun ini this year.
Besok pagi is tomorrow morning and besok malam tomorrow night. The day after tomorrow is lusa.

items.pitfallNote: In speech kemarin often means any recent day, 'the other day', not only yesterday.

items.registerNotes: Sekarang juga means 'right now, this minute'. It also means 'these days': Sekarang saya tinggal di Jakarta.
Nanti saja is 'later, not now', and nanti malam is tonight. It only looks forward: for earlier today, say tadi.
items.cultureNote: Nanti can be minutes or days away. If you need a time, ask Jam berapa?

items.registerNotes: From dawn until about 11 a.m.: Selamat pagi. After a time it does the work of a.m.: jam tujuh pagi, 7 a.m.
From about 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., the hottest part of the day: Selamat siang. Makan siang is lunch.
From about 3 p.m. until dark: Selamat sore. Jam empat sore is 4 p.m.
items.pitfallNote: Nothing to do with English 'sore'. It's two syllables, so-re, with the e as in 'bed'.

items.registerNotes: From dark, about 6 p.m.: Selamat malam. Makan malam is dinner, and jam delapan malam is 8 p.m.
Jam berapa? asks the time. Tickets and announcements say pukul instead: pukul tujuh.
items.pitfallNote: Order matters: jam tiga is three o'clock, but tiga jam is three hours.
items.cultureNote: Jam karet, 'rubber time', is the half-joking name for times that stretch: social plans often start late.

items.registerNotes: Lima menit lagi is 'in five minutes'. Ten past three is jam tiga lewat sepuluh (menit).
Usually with hari: hari Senin. The week runs Senin, Selasa, Rabu, Kamis, Jumat, Sabtu, Minggu.

items.pitfallNote: Saturday night is malam Minggu ('Sunday eve'), the big night out; Minggu malam is Sunday night.

items.registerNotes: Often just Minggu, with a capital M. With a small m, minggu is a week.
